title: T07 — Adopt upstream pending-case detection so new or changed packs raise a run
goal: Use Gauntlet's consumer-agnostic `pending` command and ledger (gauntlet-protocol F-010) and the harness evaluation-dependency setting (project-harness F-052) so new or changed cases raise a backlog item; NERV owns only its ledger, configuration and rule
acceptance: Pin the Gauntlet release that ships `pending` and `ledger record`; NERV keeps its run ledger (metadata only) in the repository
`.harness.json` declares Gauntlet as an evaluation dependency whose pending command covers every consumed pack, so check:freshness reports pending cases at session start
npm run check:gauntlet-runs (the same command) fails CI while a pending case has no open backlog item naming it (owner decision recorded: fail, not only warn)
An impact row on vendor/gauntlet-protocol.json and evals/gauntlet/** tells the agent to raise or update that item in the PR that bumps the pin
No comparison logic written in NERV; until both upstream releases exist, this task waits
privacy: Neutral synthetic cases and private local reports only; no secrets, downloads or production effects.
validation: A NERV join test: the vendored release, the ledger and the harness setting give the expected pending list for a fixture pin
escalation: Upstream dependencies: voidbrain/gauntlet-protocol F-010 and voidbrain/project-harness F-052 releases; reconcile the harness first, then pin Gauntlet
The run itself is an owner-approved real-model campaign; this task only raises it

effort.basis: Owner decision 2026-11-11: harness and Gauntlet are reused by future projects, so the comparison moves upstream (Gauntlet F-010, about 1.5 days; harness F-052, about 1 day) and NERV only adopts it. Estimate, not a measurement.
